summary: Encrypt backup credential receipts at rest (AES-256-GCM, per-host random key file, pool/host/reference as authenticated data), keep the SMB3 mount password only in a transient root-only tmpfs file, and accept a validated SMB3 domain through the web form, Controller offer validation, Core scope validation and the mount credential file. API impact: changed contract; the backup credential handoff accepts an optional domain for SMB3.

guide.reason: Operators see a Domain field for SMB3, the domain rules, encrypted credential storage and the reboot limitation.

api.reason: POST /api/v1/storage/credentials accepts an optional domain for backup SMB3 handoffs (validated identically by Controller and Core); S3 and SFTP still refuse it. Core's report and peer payloads are unchanged.

roadmap.reason: Resolves two open owner decisions of the backup destinations plan.

state.record: Encrypted private backup credential receipts under storage-cluster/secrets/backup, keyed by storage-cluster/secrets/backup-credential-key on each Core. The SMB3 mount password is transient on tmpfs. A fresh Controller reads redacted receipts from the Core report.
state.reason: No Controller state is added; the domain travels only in the transient credential handoff into Core's encrypted receipt.

verification.method: Focused Go tests in internal/agent, internal/vmhost and internal/controller, plus the web unit test and tsc. No lab, real mount or reboot run.
verification.limits: Simulated stores and stubbed mount commands only. After a host reboot the SMB3 backup mount is not remade until Core prepares the repository again. A mount unit written by an earlier build points at a removed credential file and must be detached once. Ordinary storage (non-backup) SMB credentials under storage-credentials are still plaintext files and are outside this change.
